 3                            QUESTION NO. NMPRC 1-(f):

 4   Q.   What is the base cost of fuel (per kWh) incorporated into SPS's existing rates?

 5   A.   Effective with the Final Order in Case No. 15-00296-UT, fuel costs are not included

 6        in SPS’s base rates. Therefore, there are no base costs of fuel incorporated into

 7        SPS’s existing rates. Please refer to Attachment ZEL-BR 1(f) for the Final Order

 8        and Recommended Decision in Case No. 15-00296-UT.

 9                            QUESTION NO. NMPRC 1-(g):

10   Q.   What is the base cost of fuel incorporated into SPS's proposed rates? Provide

11        the anticipated dollar cost of fuel for the test year and the anticipated billing

12        units expressed in kWh used to determine the base cost of fuel.

13   A.   Fuel costs are not included in SPS’s base rates. Therefore, there are no base costs

14        of fuel incorporated into SPS’s proposed rates.

 1                            QUESTION NO. NMPRC 1-(j):


 2   Q.   What is SPS's support for its position on the proposed recovery of its rate case

 3        and litigation expenses including discussion of the following:

 4           i. If SPS is seeking recovery of all or a portion of its rate case and

 5               litigation expenses, why should expenses be approved for recovery?

 6               SPS seeks to recover its rate case expenses, as well as specified regulatory

 7               expenses it incurred in recent proceedings, including the Standby Rate Case

 8               (Case No. 22-00155-UT), the 2023 Integrated Resource Plan, and the 2024

 9               and 2025 Requests for Proposals. These include legal fees, internal labor,

10               and payments to third-party facilitators and independent monitors. SPS

11               proposes to amortize these costs over two years. I explain these expenses

12               and the proposed amortization period in my direct testimony on pages 53-

13               73. These expenses arise from proceedings the Commission requires or

14               oversees, and that SPS must participate in, to plan its system, procure

15               resources, and provide electric service to customers. Thus, the expenses are

16               reasonable and necessary for SPS to serve customers.




                                              9

                                Zoë E. Lees

 1   ii. If SPS is seeking recovery of the expenses incurred with appeals of rate

 2      case decisions, why should these expenses be approved for recovery?

 3      SPS does not seek to recover in this case any expenses it may incur if a party

 4      appeals the Commission’s decision. SPS instead asks the Commission, if an

 5      appeal occurs, to allow SPS to record those expenses in a regulatory asset.

 6      If the Commission authorizes that treatment, SPS proposes that the deferred

 7      balance accrue interest at its approved WACC. SPS would then seek

 8      authorization to recover the costs in its next base rate case.

 9   iii. If SPS is seeking any portion of the rate case expense be included in

10      rate base, is SPS also seeking a return on the expenses? If so, why

11      should a return be authorized on the expense, and what return should

12      be authorized?

13      SPS does not ask the Commission to place rate case or other regulatory

14      expenses in rate base and does not seek a return on those expenses in this

15      proceeding.




                                      10
                                      Case No. 25-00079-UT

 1           iv. Should rate case expenses and litigation expenses be treated similarly

 2               or differently for ratemaking purposes? Provide support for your

 3               position.

 4               SPS treats rate case expenses and other regulatory proceeding expenses

 5               similarly for ratemaking purposes. Both types of expenses arise from

 6               proceedings the Commission requires or oversees, and that SPS must

 7               participate in, to plan, procure resources, and provide electric service to

 8               customers. SPS therefore proposes to amortize these costs as regulatory

 9               expenses rather than include them in rate base.

2    Q.   Are any of the costs SPS proposes to allocate solely to the New Mexico

3         jurisdiction the result of SPS's efforts to comply with New Mexico's Energy

4         Transition Act? If so, what are the costs for ETA compliance for New Mexico

5         retail customers?

6    A.   SPS is not proposing to allocate any costs solely to the New Mexico jurisdiction as

7         a direct result of SPS’s efforts to comply with the New Mexico Energy Transition

8         Act. SPS proposes in this case to directly assign and allocate solely to New Mexico

9         costs associated with the Cunningham Battery Energy Storage System (“BESS”).

10        SPS may request that the Cunningham BESS be considered in Renewable Portfolio

11        Standard compliance in the future, but compliance with the ETA is not the reason

12        for requesting direct assignment in this case.

14   A.   Yes.

        Anthony Medeiros, Hearing Examiner in this case, presents this Certification of

Stipulation (“Certification”) to the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission

(“Commission”) in accordance with Rule 1.2.2.20(A)(5)(b) NMAC. This Certification

concerns the Unanimous Comprehensive Stipulation (“Stipulation”) entered into by

Southwestern Public Service Company (“SPS”), the Utility Division Staff of the

Commission (“Staff”), Hector H. Balderas, the Attorney General of New Mexico (“AG”),

Occidental Permian Ltd. (“OPL”), Federal Executive Agencies (“FEA”), Louisiana Energy

Services LLC d/b/a/ URENCO USA (“LES”), Lea County, New Mexico Gas Company

(“NMGC”), Vote Solar, and the Coalition for Clean Affordable Energy (“CCAE”)

(collectively, the “Signatories”). The Signatories’ filing made on May 2, 2016 asserts that

the Stipulation resolves and settles all issues in this case and recommends that the

Commission approve and adopt it.          A copy of the Stipulation is attached to this

Certification as Appendix A.

  I.    STATEMENT OF THE CASE

        SPS initiated this base rate case on September 16, 2015 with the filing of a verified

motion for a protective order, requesting that the Commission issue a protective order to

govern the filing, disclosure, and use of confidential, competitively sensitive, or proprietary

information in the case. On September 30, 2015, the Commission issued an order which

both granted SPS’s motion and incorporated the Protective Order.

        On October 7, 2015, SPS filed a motion for admission of Stephen Fogel to appear in

exclusive ratemaking authority to the Commission, and the Commission is vested with

substantial discretion in determining the reasonableness of utility rates.22 With regard to
